title: Design System: Business Ledger — Landing (Switchboard World)

display.purpose: Hero headline only, set in Big Shoulders Display.

headline.purpose: Section h2 headings across the page.

title.purpose: Feature-row h3 headings and the sign-in card heading.

body.purpose: Running copy, always cream-dim on the dark ground.

label.purpose: Engraved brass-plate captions beside jacks, lamps, and feature tags — never above a heading.

mono.purpose: Every dollar figure and business-name data caption; never headlines or body.

shadows.name: panel-mount
shadows.purpose: Standard raised-insert treatment for hero card, sign-in card, feature strip, mechanism readout.

shadows.name: screenshot-mount
shadows.purpose: Screenshot window mount, slightly lighter than card-level panel-mount.

shadows.name: lamp-glow-active
shadows.purpose: Ambient glow on a Lamp primitive when active; absent at rest.

shadows.name: jack-active-ring
shadows.purpose: Glow ring layered over the fixed-material jack photo when a jack is active.

motion.name: section-reveal
motion.purpose: The one authored section-entrance moment, used by the Section wrapper.

motion.name: cable-spring
motion.purpose: Patch cable draw-in, mechanical/damped per the direction contract.

motion.name: ticker-easeout
motion.purpose: TickerTotal's adding-machine climb to its value.

motion.name: seat-flash
motion.purpose: One-shot ring pulse fired when a jack transitions to active; timed to the component's real 550ms setTimeout.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Sign In / form submit — the only filled action in the system.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #3ecf8e; color: #0c0906; padding: 10px 20px; border-radius: 8px; font-weight: 500; font-size: 14px; font-family: 'Big Shoulders Text', sans-serif; border: none; transition: transform 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(1.05); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.98); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #e3c383; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.6; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary in-page-anchor action, e.g. 'See it work'.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: #ece0c8; padding: 10px 20px; border-radius: 8px; font-weight: 500; font-size: 14px; font-family: 'Big Shoulders Text', sans-serif; border: none; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(184,147,90,0.22); } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(184,147,90,0.4); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #e3c383; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Input Field
components.css: .ds-input { background: #0c0906; color: #ece0c8; padding: 10px 12px; border-radius: 8px; border: none; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(184,147,90,0.22); font-family: 'Big Shoulders Text', sans-serif; font-size: 14px; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #e3c383; outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Plate Label
components.description: Engraved brass-plate caption grammar; sits beside content, never above a heading.
components.css: .ds-plate-label { display: inline-block; font-family: 'Big Shoulders Display', sans-serif; font-weight: 500; font-size: 11px; letter-spacing: 0.18em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #b8935a; }

components.name: Panel Card
components.description: The system's one card shape: photographed-texture-under-tint surface with brass corner screws.
components.html: Sign in
components.css: .ds-panel { position: relative; border-radius: 12px; padding: 24px; background: linear-gradient(165deg, rgba(31,23,14,0.86), rgba(12,9,6,0.93)); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(184,147,90,0.35), 0 20px 50px rgba(0,0,0,0.55); } .ds-panel-title { font-family: 'Big Shoulders Display', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 24px; color: #ece0c8; margin: 0; } .ds-screw { position: absolute; width: 14px; height: 14px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #6e5936; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.7); } .ds-screw-tl { top: 6px; left: 6px; } .ds-screw-tr { top: 6px; right: 6px; } .ds-screw-bl { bottom: 6px; left: 6px; } .ds-screw-br { bottom: 6px; right: 6px; }

components.name: Jack + Lamp
components.description: Signature component: a socket whose fixed-material photo never changes color, plus a separate glow-ring and idle/active lamp for state.
components.css: .ds-jack-wrap { position: relative; width: 30px; height: 30px; border-radius: 9999px; background: radial-gradient(circle, #4a3a24, #1a130a); } .ds-jack-ring { position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 9999px; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px rgba(62,207,142,0.67), inset 0 0 9px rgba(62,207,142,0.33), 0 0 13px rgba(62,207,142,0.33); } .ds-lamp { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #3a2f1e; margin-top: 8px; } .ds-lamp-active { background: #f4a623; box-shadow: 0 0 12px 4px rgba(244,166,35,0.4), 0 0 4px #f4a623; }

narrative.overview: The landing page is a single near-black bakelite patch panel, not a page of floating text over a gradient wash. Every surface — hero, feature strip, screenshot mounts, the sign-in card — is a physical insert bolted into the same panel material with real brass screws at its corners. Business identity is expressed as jacks on a trunk line: three businesses patch into one master total, and isolating a single business means literally unplugging the others rather than filtering a list. This is a fixed dark world; it is not part of the app's own light/dark-toggleable theme and does not inherit or export tokens to it. This is the shipped result of a rebuild pass, not the first draft. The first attempt centered a floating text stack in the hero (rejected — contradicts the panel-as-hero contract), used a same-size icon+heading+text card grid for the features section (rejected — the world's own line is a continuous trunk, not a card grid), and rendered every panel as a flat CSS gradient (rejected — the world's own material is bakelite/brass, and flat gradient does not read as that material). All three were rebuilt before this record was written.
keyCharacteristics: One continuous panel material (photographed texture + tint), never a flat gradient standing in for it.
Jacks, cables, and lamps as the literal visual grammar for "business" / "connection" / "active state."
Brass-plate labels sit beside headings, never above them, at every breakpoint.
Emerald reads income/active, rust-red reads expense, amber reads an idle lamp turning on.
Tabular figures are always Space Mono; running copy and headlines are never set in it.

rules.name: The Two-Signal Rule
rules.body: Only emerald and rust-red carry semantic meaning (positive/negative, active/isolated). Amber is reserved exclusively for the lamp's own idle→active transition and never doubles as a third semantic color.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-For-Numbers Rule
rules.body: Space Mono renders only figures and short data captions (dollar totals, business-name tags under jacks). It never sets a headline, a body paragraph, or a label — monospace here means "measurement," not "technical" costume.

rules.name: The Material-Before-Gradient Rule
rules.body: No panel surface is a flat CSS gradient. Every panel, card, and inset layers a photographed texture (bakelite grain or brass screw/jack photography) under a semi-transparent color tint via panelSurface(); the tint sets mood, the photograph supplies material.

dos: Do build every panel surface with panelSurface() (photographed texture + tint gradient) — never a flat CSS gradient standing in for bakelite or brass.

Do keep plate labels (PlateLabel) positioned beside their heading or content, using DOM order plus responsive order classes so the label never sits above the heading at any breakpoint, including mobile stack.
Do reserve Space Mono strictly for figures and short data captions; set headlines and body copy in Big Shoulders.
Do give every shadow real offset and blur (see the Panel-mount vocabulary); depth communicates through blur and material layering, not flat halos.
Do draw icons as authored SVG (e.g. the chevron) in a single consistent stroke weight — never a Unicode glyph or emoji.
donts: Don't use a same-size icon+heading+text card grid for feature sections. This world's features are one continuous hairline-divided terminal strip off a shared trunk, not independent cards — the original build did this and was rebuilt.

Don't place a kicker/eyebrow label directly above a heading at any breakpoint. Plate labels sit beside content via flex-order, never stacked above it — two instances of the banned pattern were found and repositioned during finish review.

Don't render a panel, card, or inset as a flat CSS gradient with no photographed material underneath. Three surfaces shipped this way originally (hero, panels, jack sockets) and were rebuilt with real texture/photo assets.

Don't bake active-state color into a jack's own socket material. State lives in the separate glow-ring layered on top of a fixed-material photograph, matching how a real jack's metal doesn't change color while its indicator lamp does.
Don't use a hard-offset, zero-blur shadow anywhere in this system. It was never adopted and does not belong to this material world.
